clue.text: Top notes audible in the main

indicators.note: audible tells us the clue words are to be heard spoken, not read

parts.note: high Cs are notes at the top of a singer's range

explanation.surface: A singer's high notes ring out somewhere in the main body of a concert.
explanation.walkthrough: 'High Cs' and the answer sound alike. 'The main' is the old poetic term for the open ocean, not 'main' as in principal.
explanation.definitionFit: The main is a literary name for the open ocean, the waters beyond any nation's territory.

clue.text: City integral to Bahai faith

indicators.note: integral to says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A city central to the Baha'i religion.
explanation.definitionFit: Haifa is a port in northern Israel, home of the Baha'i World Centre, which makes the surface true.

clue.text: With seabird circling, I get book to look up 'auk'

indicators.note: circling means going round the I

parts.note: a gull is a seabird

indicators.note: to look up means the word reads upward, backwards in a down answer

parts.note: a tome is a large book

explanation.surface: A birdwatcher with gulls wheeling overhead consults a guide to identify an auk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'circling' and 'to look up' are the indicators; in a down answer 'look up' means read from bottom to top. The quotes on 'auk' mark it as the definition, a family name rather than a single bird.
explanation.definitionFit: This black-and-white cliff-nesting seabird belongs to the auk family, so it is an example.

clue.text: Russian vessel to circulate endlessly in western European river

indicators.note: in puts the shortened word inside the river

parts.note: the Saar flows through France and Germany

indicators.note: endlessly means the last letter is cut off

parts.note: to move about is to circulate

explanation.surface: A Russian ship sailing round and round a river in western Europe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endlessly' trims the last letter and 'in' sets the result inside the river. 'Vessel' suggests a ship but means a container.
explanation.definitionFit: This is an urn for boiling water for tea, traditional in Russia, so a Russian container.

clue.text: Looks at a TV screen — it's broken

indicators.note: broken means the letters are smashed and reassembled

explanation.surface: Someone peers at a TV and finds the screen broken.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broken' rearranges AT A TV SCREEN plus IT'S. 'Looks' seems a verb but is the noun: good looks.
explanation.definitionFit: Good looks are physical beauty, the quality of being appealing to the eye.

clue.text: Mass behind stadium ends missing logo

indicators.note: behind places the mass letter after the trimmed stadium
ends missing says the stadium's first and last letters are dropped

parts.note: Wembley is the national football stadium in London
M is the physics abbreviation for mass

explanation.surface: A club's badge is missing from the ends of the stadium, behind which a crowd gathers.
explanation.walkthrough: Wembley is London's national football stadium; 'ends missing' strips its first and last letters, and 'behind' puts the mass letter after.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are a symbol or badge standing for an organisation, so they are synonyms.

clue.text: It'll remind me to put sex first

indicators.note: first places the sex word before 'to'

parts.note: taken as written
men are one sex
taken as written

explanation.surface: A note to self to prioritise one's love life.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put ... first' places the sex word ahead of 'to'; 'men' as one sex is a common crossword shortcut.
explanation.definitionFit: A keepsake serves as a reminder of a person or event, so it is something that reminds.

clue.text: I'll enter name coming up for tree

indicators.note: coming up means reading upward, backwards in a down answer
enter means the I goes inside the name word

parts.note: to call is to name
I will, so the letter I is the one entering

explanation.surface: Someone vows to put a name forward for a tree.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I'll enter' puts I into CALL (CALIL); 'coming up' reverses it in a down answer.
explanation.definitionFit: This lilac-flowered shrub can grow into a small tree, so it is an example.

clue.text: Malicious act involving end of cigar resulting in wound

indicators.note: involving means the deed wraps around the cigar's last letter

parts.note: a mean deed is a spiteful act

indicators.note: end of picks out the final letter of the following word

explanation.surface: A spiteful act with a lit cigar causes an injury.
explanation.walkthrough: 'involving' puts R inside MEAN DEED. 'Wound' rhymes with 'round', not 'tuned': the past tense of wind.
explanation.definitionFit: To wind is to twist and turn along a course, so a river that wound took a winding path.

clue.text: A cold needs not to spread — get a tissue

parts.note: a chill is a cold

indicators.note: to spread means the letters are scattered into a new order

explanation.surface: Advice for stopping a cold from spreading: grab a tissue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to spread' rearranges NEEDS NOT. 'Tissue' suggests a hanky but is body tissue.
explanation.definitionFit: This tough band of fibrous tissue joins the calf muscles to the heel bone.

clue.text: Foolish to cling to degree of particularity in language

indicators.note: to cling to says the foolish word wraps itself around the degree

parts.note: idiotic means foolish
an MA is a Master of Arts degree

explanation.surface: A daft insistence on hair-splitting precision in language.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to cling to' wraps the foolish word around the degree. The definition starts at 'of', reading as an adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom is phrasing peculiar to a language, so an expression natural to its native speakers has that particularity.

clue.text: Island whisky's ace

parts.note: malt is a single-malt whisky
A is the card abbreviation for ace

explanation.surface: An island's whisky is its trump card.
explanation.definitionFit: Malta is a Mediterranean island nation south of Sicily.

clue.text: Making light of computers and artificial intelligence in book from the east

indicators.note: from the east means reading right to left, westward, in an across answer
in places the computers and AI letters inside the book

parts.note: a novella is a short novel
IT, information technology, stands for computers

explanation.surface: Someone trivialising tech and AI in a book written from an eastern viewpoint.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts ITAI inside NOVELLA after NO, giving NOITAIVELLA; 'from the east' reverses that whole string.
explanation.definitionFit: Relief makes a burden lighter, so lessening pain or worry is a making light of it.

clue.text: You'll pay for that joke

definitions.meaning: cash on delivery: payment is taken when the goods arrive
... in British slang means mock or sham, as in a ... accent

explanation.surface: A threat of revenge after a bad gag.
explanation.walkthrough: COD, cash on delivery, means you pay as goods arrive; 'cod' as an adjective is British slang for fake or parody.
explanation.definitionFit: Cash on delivery is a payment arrangement; and a fake or parody thing is a mere jest, a sham.

clue.text: What's inside leg measurement — perhaps moleskin trousers?

indicators.note: trousers as a verb means pockets, so the fur takes the measurement inside it

parts.note: moleskin is an example of fur, the pelt of a mole
an em is a printer's unit of measurement

explanation.surface: An inside-leg measurement for a pair of moleskin trousers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trousers' is a verb: FUR pockets EM, a printer's measure.
explanation.definitionFit: The thigh bone is the long bone running through the upper leg, so it lies inside a leg.

clue.text: Anticipation of conflict about valuable resources

indicators.note: about means going round the resources

parts.note: a fight is a conflict
ores are mined mineral resources

explanation.surface: Foreseeing a war over valuable natural resources.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' wraps the conflict word round the resources; 'of' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are the ability to predict and prepare for what will happen, so they are synonyms.

clue.text: Group of animals including giraffes perhaps facing tough task

definitions.text: Group of animals including giraffes perhaps
definitions.meaning: an order is a rank of animal classification, and giraffes are lofty, so a lofty order would include them
a demanding job that is hard to carry out

explanation.surface: Herding giraffes into a group would be a tough job.
explanation.walkthrough: The first reading is whimsical: ORDER is a classification rank, and an order of giraffes would be a lofty one.
explanation.definitionFit: This idiom names a request or job that is unreasonably difficult to fulfil.

clue.text: Two characters heard at the same time in first half of Mousetrap

definitions.text: Two characters heard at the same time in first half of Mousetrap

parts.words: Two characters heard at the same time in first half of Mousetrap
parts.note: the OU of mouse is two vowels sounding as one gliding sound; the surface suggests two actors in Agatha Christie's play

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests two actors on stage together in The Mousetrap, Agatha Christie's long-running London play; the 'characters' are letters, the O and U in MOUSE.
explanation.definitionFit: This phonetics term names two vowel sounds gliding together in one syllable, like OU in house.

clue.text: After avalanche, I run Everest rescues

indicators.note: after an avalanche everything has tumbled into disorder, so these letters are jumbled

parts.note: I as written, R the cricket abbreviation for run, and Everest as written

explanation.surface: A mountain rescuer describing their work on Everest after an avalanche.
explanation.walkthrough: 'After avalanche' signals the anagram of I, R and EVEREST.
explanation.definitionFit: To recover or bring back something lost, a synonym of saving or recovering.

clue.text: Guts sardine, after cutting off tail, to stew with end of lemon

indicators.note: to stew means the letters are cooked into a new mixture
cutting off tail means the last letter of the fish is dropped
end of picks out the final letter of the following word

explanation.surface: A cooking instruction: gut a sardine, cut off its tail, and stew it with lemon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to stew' rearranges SARDIN (sardine with tail cut off) plus N. 'Guts' looks like a verb but is the noun.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are informal words for the entrails, the internal organs of the body.

clue.text: Tasty food like hummus, say, returned

indicators.note: returned means the letters come back the other way

parts.note: hummus is an example of a dip
as can mean for example, like say

explanation.surface: Someone praising a dish of hummus they sent back to the kitchen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returned' reverses DIP + AS (DIPAS).
explanation.definitionFit: A rare word for having a pleasant, savoury flavour, so a synonym of flavoursome.

clue.text: Dish in sink

definitions.meaning: to dish chances is to ruin or wreck them
to deliberately sink one's own ship by holing it

explanation.surface: A plate left in the kitchen basin.
explanation.definitionFit: To wreck a plan or to sink a ship by holing it are both meanings of this verb.

clue.text: Very soft piece of bread

parts.note: so means very, as in so good
P is the music abbreviation for piano, soft

explanation.surface: A description of an extremely soft slice of bread.
explanation.definitionFit: A morsel of bread dipped in soup or gravy is called this.

clue.text: Excited after getting private number for model

indicators.note: after getting places the excited word after the number

parts.note: a PIN is a personal identification number, kept private
up means excited, as in being up for it

explanation.surface: Someone thrilled to get a model's private phone number.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after getting' puts the excited word second; 'up' as excited, as in 'feeling up'.
explanation.definitionFit: A glamour model whose picture is stuck on walls is called this.

clue.text: Bizarre question in reversed sequence that doesn't follow

indicators.note: in puts the mixed-up letters inside the backwards sequence word
reversed says the sequence word is turned backwards

parts.note: a run is a sequence, as of cards or wins

indicators.note: bizarre suggests something weird, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the anagram fodder as written

explanation.surface: An odd question arising in a jumbled-up order, out of logical sequence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bizarre' shuffles QUESTION into ONSEQUIT, and 'in' places it inside NUR, the sequence word 'reversed'. The definition is a noun phrase: a remark that doesn't follow.
explanation.definitionFit: Latin for 'it does not follow', this names a conclusion or remark unconnected to what went before.

clue.text: Lee's partner for cider or tea

definitions.text: Lee's partner for cider or tea

parts.words: Lee's partner for cider or tea
parts.note: Cider with ... is Laurie Lee's memoir, and ... Lee is Cockney rhyming slang for tea

explanation.walkthrough: Two British references: Cider with Rosie is Laurie Lee's memoir of a Cotswold childhood, and Rosie Lee is Cockney rhyming slang for tea.
explanation.definitionFit: A girl's name that pairs with Lee as rhyming slang for tea and appears in the title of his cider memoir.

clue.text: Promiscuous type embracing navy chap who's hopeless

indicators.note: embracing means holding the navy letter inside

parts.note: a goer is slang for a sexually adventurous person

explanation.surface: A hopeless sailor clinging to a flirt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'embracing' puts N inside GOER.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone beyond help or doomed is described in slang as a lost cause, past saving.

clue.text: Suspicion surrounds publication without name that promotes disorder

indicators.note: surrounds puts the suspicion letters around the shortened publication

parts.note: sus is British slang for suspicion, as in arrested on sus

indicators.note: without means the name letter is left out

parts.note: an edition is a published version of a book or paper

explanation.surface: A suspicious-looking anonymous pamphlet that stirs up rebellion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' drops the name letter, leaving EDITIO; 'surrounds' splits the slang word for suspicion around it. Sus is British police slang.
explanation.definitionFit: This describes speech or writing inciting rebellion against the state, so it encourages unrest.

clue.text: Key worker reported Asian drunk

indicators.note: reported says we hear the words said, not spell them

parts.note: a Thai is someone from Thailand, and pissed is British slang for drunk

explanation.surface: A frontline worker is said to be an inebriated Asian man.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pissed' is British slang for drunk; 'Thai pissed' said aloud matches the answer. 'Key worker' is a pun: one who works keys.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone whose job is typing works at a keyboard, pressing keys all day.

clue.text: Give line designed to persuade

indicators.note: designed means arranged in a new pattern, so the letters are reworked

explanation.surface: Delivering a well-crafted line to win someone over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'designed' rearranges GIVE LINE.
explanation.definitionFit: To coax or win someone over by flattery or trickery, a crafty kind of persuasion.
